![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14057969/assets/34b4b349b8295ee6443a85f019f6bf5e7ea6c6aafe9109ac7935610e6aefcacf.png)

Which of the following gives the line integral ${\int }_{C}(25-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is three-quarters of the ellipse $36{x}^{2}+25{y}^{2}=900,$ shown above?
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{6}^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $5$ and $6,$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(6\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25{sin}^{2}⁡t+36{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{11{cos}^{2}⁡t+25({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{11{cos}^{2}⁡t+25}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=25-{x}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =25-(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2} \\  & =25-25{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =25(1-{cos}^{2}⁡t) \\  & =25{sin}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(25-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }25{sin}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{11{cos}^{2}⁡t+25}\,\text{d}t \\  & =25{\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{11{cos}^{2}⁡t+25}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
